dedupe_keys.name: geomechanical modeling for thermal spallation drilling

description: Geomechanical Modeling for Thermal Spallation Drilling is a dataset listed in Open Energy Hub (ORNL), an energy-sector data hub, published or maintained by Oak Ridge National Laboratory for the U.S. DOE Office of Electricity. Wells for Engineered Geothermal Systems (EGS) typically occur in conditions presenting significant challenges for conventional rotary and percussive drilling technologies: granitic rocks that reduce drilling speeds and cause substantial equipment wear. Thermal spallation drilling, in which rock is fragmented by high temperature, not mechanical means, offers a potential solution to these problems. Coverage: the United States. The portal files it under Geothermal Energy. Its keywords are geothermal, geomechanical modeling, thermal spallation drilling, geodyn, numerical modeling, engineered geothermal system (egs). The portal shows 2017-05-23 as the last modification. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support network planning and operations studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-oeh-open-data-portal.
